surfaces: Interactive CLI (`qwen`), non-interactive CLI (`qwen -p`), VS Code "Qwen Code IDE Companion" extension, ACP bridge / daemon (`qwen serve`). The IDE companion does NOT use VS Code `globalStorage/state.vscdb` — a full-text search of the published 0.25.3 bundle for `state.vscdb` and `globalStorage` returns ZERO hits. The extension talks to the daemon/ACP bridge over the wire, so no SQLite dependency is needed for a Discodex adapter.
binaries: `qwen` (npm bin -> `dist/index.js`; on Windows the shim is `qwen.cmd` / `qwen.ps1`; there is no native `qwen.exe` in the npm package, so `Provider::from_executable` must accept "qwen" AND "qwen.cmd"). The CLI sets its terminal/window title to `Qwen - <folderName>` (env `CLI_TITLE` override, `DEFAULT_WINDOW_TITLE = "qwen"`), and on win32 assigns `process.title` — so `Provider::from_window` should match a title equal to "qwen" or starting with "qwen - ".

paths: %USERPROFILE%\.qwen\projects\<sanitized-cwd>\workflows\<runId>\journal.jsonl   (workflow resume journal, NOT a chat log — must be excluded)
storage.format: JSONL — one self-contained JSON object per line, newline-terminated. NOT JSON-per-file, NOT SQLite, NOT Markdown, NOT protobuf, NOT encrypted. Every line is a `ChatRecord` with `uuid`/`parentUuid` (tree-structured history), `sessionId`, ISO-8601 `timestamp`, `type`, `cwd`, `version`, optional `model`, optional `message.parts` (role + text/functionCall/functionResponse/thought parts), optional `toolCallResult` metadata, optional `systemPayload`, optional `agentId`/`agentName`/`isSidechain`.
storage.append_semantics: PURELY APPEND-ONLY, LIVE. `jsonl.writeLine()` does `fs.promises.appendFile(filePath, Buffer.from(json + "\n"), { flush: true })` under a per-file mutex — one fsync'd line per record, written as the agent works. The file is created once with `writeFileSync(path, '', {flag:'wx'})` and then only appended to; it is never rewritten wholesale. `jsonl.write()` (atomic full-file overwrite) exists in the codebase but is NOT used by the chat recorder. This matches the Discodex `LogTailer` model exactly — no watcher changes needed.
storage.session_file_naming: `<sessionId>.jsonl` where sessionId is a UUIDv4 (regex `^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[1-5][0-9a-f]{3}-[89ab][0-9a-f]{3}-[0-9a-f]{12}(-agent-[a-zA-Z0-9_.-]+)?$`); the `-agent-<name>` suffix marks Arena sub-agent sessions. One file per logical session.

fields.project: RECOVERABLE. Every record carries a top-level `cwd` = `config.getProjectRoot()` = the directory the CLI was launched in (the workspace root). Publish only its final path segment (folder name) — the same rule Discodex already applies to Codex/Claude. NOTE: the on-disk project directory name is `sanitizeCwd(cwd)` = on Windows lowercased path with every non-alphanumeric char replaced by '-', e.g. `C:\Users\PC\Documents\Discodex` -> `c--users-pc-documents-discodex`. That is lossy (dashes are ambiguous) so use the record's `cwd` field, never the directory name.
fields.model: RECOVERABLE. Assistant records carry `model` (e.g. `qwen3-coder-plus`) and `executionContext.modelId`. A `type:"system", subtype:"session_model"` record carries `systemPayload.modelId` (+ `authType`, optional `baseUrl`, `isRuntime`) for the last-wins session model. Sanitize to a strict `[A-Za-z0-9._:/@-]`, <=128 chars before publishing.
fields.file_basename: RECOVERABLE from the tool-call args. `read_file`, `write_file` and `edit` all take `file_path`; `glob`/`grep_search` take optional `path`; `list_directory` takes `path`; `run_shell_command`/`exec` take `command` (no path). Discodex's existing `extract_file_basename()` already probes `path`, `file`, `file_path`, `filepath` — `file_path` and `path` cover every Qwen file-bearing tool. Publish basename only.
fields.tool_activity: RECOVERABLE, and the richest of the four existing adapters. The assistant record's `message.parts[]` contains `functionCall { id, name, args }` — `name` is the canonical tool name (`read_file`, `write_file`, `edit`, `glob`, `grep_search`, `list_directory`, `run_shell_command`, `exec`, `lsp`, `web_fetch`, `web_search`, `agent`, `todo_write`, `notebook_edit`, `ask_user_question`, ...), `args` is the raw argument object, and `id` is the call id. Legacy aliases exist (`replace`->`edit`, `search_file_content`->`grep_search`, `task`->`agent`) and are mapped by `canonicalToolName()`. Tool completion is a separate `type:"tool_result"` record whose `message.parts[]` carry `functionResponse { id, name, response }` plus a `toolCallResult { callId, displayName, status }` metadata object. The `functionCall.id` / `functionResponse.id` pair is exactly what `TrackedToolStarted`/`TrackedToolFinished` need.
fields.phase: RECOVERABLE. Turn boundaries: (a) START = a `type:"user"` record with `provenance:"real_user"` and NO `subtype` (the real user prompt; note `subtype:"notification"` records are provenance `system`, and `agent_mention`/`agent_message` are provenance `external_agent`, so those must be excluded); (b) END = a `type:"system", subtype:"turn_result"` record (settled turn, bounded payload); (c) a resumed attempt writes `subtype:"turn_attempt"`. Tool-running vs thinking is derived from the interleaving of `functionCall` and `functionResponse` parts, exactly like the existing Claude/Antigravity adapters.
fields.timestamps: RECOVERABLE. Every record has top-level `timestamp` = `new Date().toISOString()` (UTC, RFC-3339 with milliseconds, e.g. `2026-10-21T07:17:16.123Z`). Discodex's existing `line_timestamp_ms()` already probes the top-level `timestamp` key and `timestamp_ms()` already parses RFC-3339, so historical replay gets correct per-line `now_ms` for free. Records are strictly append-ordered (single writer, mutex-serialized).

parser_strategy:
New function `parse_qwen_line(line) -> Vec<ParsedEvent>` in src/events.rs, wired into `parse_line_for` as `Provider::QwenCode => parse_qwen_line(line)`. It parses ONE line as a `serde_json::Value` and never looks at the line as text.

Record dispatch (on `type` + `subtype` + `provenance`):
- `type == "user"` AND `subtype` is absent AND `provenance == "real_user"`  -> `ParsedEvent::TaskStarted { started_at_ms }` using the record's own `timestamp` (RFC-3339 -> ms; fall back to `now_ms`).
- `type == "assistant"` -> walk `message.parts[]`:
    * part.functionCall present -> for each: `ParsedEvent::TrackedToolStarted { call_id: functionCall.id, activity }` where `activity.label = classify_tool(&canonical_name.to_ascii_lowercase(), command)` and `activity.file = extract_file_basename(functionCall.args)`, `activity.language = language_from_file(file)`. `classify_tool()` and `extract_file_basename()` ALREADY exist in events.rs and already handle Qwen's names: `read_file` -> "Reading project files", `write_file`/`edit` -> "Editing files" (the `name == "edit"` branch), `grep_search`/`glob` -> "Searching project", `list_directory` -> "Reading project files" (matches `name.contains("list")`), `run_shell_command` -> the command branch (the `name.contains("shell")` / `contains("command")` arm) so `cargo test` -> "Running Rust tests", `git diff` -> "Reviewing repository", etc.
    * part is a plain `text` part (or a `thought` part) and the record has NO functionCall -> `ParsedEvent::TerminalCandidate` (the assistant produced a final answer). DO NOT read the text.
    * part is a `thought` part -> `ParsedEvent::Thinking { reasoning: None }` only. DO NOT publish the thought text (it is model output; the hard privacy rule forbids assistant responses).
    * assistant record with `model` set -> `ParsedEvent::AgentDetected { agent }` with the model id run through a strict charset/length filter (mirror `deepseek_model_label`).
- `type == "tool_result"` -> `ParsedEvent::TrackedToolFinished { call_id }` where call_id = `toolCallResult.callId`, else the `message.parts[].functionResponse.id`. Never read `functionResponse.response`.
- `type == "system"`:
    * `subtype == "turn_result"` -> `ParsedEvent::Completed` (turn settled).
    * `subtype == "turn_attempt"` -> ignore (a resumed attempt, not a new turn start).
    * `subtype == "session_model"` -> `ParsedEvent::AgentDetected { agent }` from `systemPayload.modelId` (sanitized).
    * `subtype == "parent_session"` -> ignore for now (see risks).
    * anything else (chat_compression, file_history_snapshot, slash_command, ui_telemetry, at_command, notification, agent_bootstrap, goal_*, branch_checkpoint, managed_session_*) -> ignore.
- EVERY record: if `cwd` is a non-empty string, emit `ParsedEvent::SessionMetadata { project: project_name(cwd), cwd }` — `project_name()` already extracts only the last path component, so the full path stays local. Reuse `is_internal_path()`-style filtering so a cwd inside `~/.qwen` is ignored.

Alias handling: call `canonicalToolName`-equivalent mapping inline in Rust (`replace`->`edit`, `search_file_content`->`grep_search`, `task`->`agent`) before `classify_tool`, otherwise `task` would classify as "Running coding agent" via the `name.contains("agent")` arm only after mapping; mapping first keeps labels consistent with upstream.

`line_timestamp_ms()` needs NO change: it already probes the top-level `timestamp` key and `timestamp_ms()` already parses RFC-3339 strings.

The managed-engine dialect (`subtype: managed_session_header_v1` / `managed_session_event_v1` / `managed_session_commit_v1`) is a DIFFERENT schema (event kinds like `input.accepted`, `model.attempt`, `wake.requested`, `occurredAt` epoch-ms, `payload` free-form). It is only used for ACP/daemon/worktree sessions. The parser should recognize those subtypes and return an empty vec (fail safe) rather than mis-parse them.

IS_SESSION_LOG FILENAME RULE (src/provider.rs)
```rust
Provider::QwenCode => {
    // <root>/<project-id>/chats/<uuid>.jsonl
    if !lower_filename.ends_with(".jsonl") { return false; }
    let stem = lower_filename.trim_end_matches(".jsonl");
    // sessionId is a UUIDv4, optionally with the `-agent-<name>` suffix
    let is_uuid = {
        let base = stem.split("-agent-").next().unwrap_or(stem);
        base.len() == 36
            && base.chars().position(|c| c == '-') == Some(8)
            && base.split('-').count() == 5
            && base.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_hexdigit() || c == '-')
    };
    let parent_is_chats = path.parent()
        .and_then(|p| p.file_name())
        .and_then(|n| n.to_str())
        .is_some_and(|n| n.eq_ignore_ascii_case("chats"));
    is_uuid && parent_is_chats
}
```
The "parent dir must be named `chats`" clause is what excludes `<projectDir>/workflows/<runId>/journal.jsonl` and any other `.jsonl` under `~/.qwen`. The UUID-stem clause excludes stray `.jsonl` files.

WATCHER.RS / MAIN.RS CHANGES
- NONE REQUIRED for the primary path. The Qwen log is append-only, newline-delimited JSONL written with `appendFile(..., {flush:true})`, i.e. exactly the shape `LogTailer` already handles. `notify`'s recursive watch on `~/.qwen/projects` (or `~/.qwen/tmp`) fires on each append, `tailer.read_new(&path)` yields the new complete lines, and `apply_lines()` feeds `parse_line_for(Provider::QwenCode, &line)`.
- Small robustness tweak worth making in main.rs: `recent_logs` is called with `limit = 8` per source at startup. Because Qwen creates one file per session and a user may have many project dirs, 8 is fine, but consider raising the per-provider cap for QwenCode or preferring the newest file in each `chats/` dir.
- Optional enrichment (NOT required): `~/.qwen/projects/<sanitized>/chats/<sessionId>.runtime.json` is a small sidecar written by `writeRuntimeStatus()` containing `{schema_version, pid, session_id, work_dir, hostname, started_at (epoch seconds, fractional), qwen_version}`. It is explicitly documented upstream as being for "external tools (terminal multiplexers, tab managers, IDE integrations, observability daemons)" to answer "which session is PID X serving?". It is NOT deleted on `/quit` or crash, so a liveness check (does `pid` still exist?) is required. It would give a rock-solid `work_dir` and `started_at` for the elapsed timer, but it is a JSON-per-file, atomically REWRITTEN artifact, not an append-only log — so it must NOT be fed to `LogTailer`/`parse_line_for`. If used, it needs a separate small reader (a "watch this one path, re-read on change" path), i.e. it is an optional second-stage enhancement, not part of the base adapter.
- The `managed` engine dialect also lives in the same `<sessionId>.jsonl` path but is only produced for ACP/daemon/worktree sessions. The parser must recognize `managed_session_*` subtypes and return no events (fail safe) rather than mis-parse. No watcher change is needed for this either — the same append-only file/line protocol is used.

FORMAT-CHURN RISK AND FAIL-SAFE
- Risk 1 (path churn, HIGH but bounded): the chats dir moved from `~/.qwen/tmp/<sha256>/chats/` (v0.1.0-v0.3.0) to `~/.qwen/projects/<sanitizeCwd>/chats/` (v0.4.0+). Mitigation: register BOTH roots. Fail-safe: if neither root exists, `session_sources()` simply yields nothing and Discodex falls back to focused-window detection.
- Risk 2 (record-schema churn, MEDIUM): Qwen adds new `subtype`s frequently (the upstream list has 30+). Mitigation: the parser is a whitelist keyed on `type` + `subtype`; unknown subtypes return an empty vec. Never use a catch-all that forwards text.
- Risk 3 (engine split, MEDIUM): legacy ChatRecord vs `managed_session_*` in the SAME file path. Mitigation: the managed subtypes are explicitly ignored. If upstream later makes `managed` the default for plain CLI sessions, Discodex would silently lose tool granularity — so add a one-line startup log ("qwen managed-engine session detected, tool granularity unavailable") rather than failing.
- Risk 4 (root relocation, LOW): `QWEN_HOME` / `QWEN_RUNTIME_DIR` / `runtimeOutputDir` can move the tree. Fail-safe: also probe the env var, and if the default roots are absent, log it.
- Risk 5 (record format differs from Gemini CLI even though both are "JSONL"): the format is a superset of Gemini CLI's, so a future Gemini CLI adapter can share helpers. Not a risk for Qwen.
- Risk 6 (privacy): the Qwen JSONL contains the FULL prompt, assistant text, and raw tool output on disk. The adapter must never copy any of it into a `ToolActivity.label`, into `Thinking.reasoning`, or into `AgentDetected.agent`. All labels must come from the closed `classify_tool()` table; all file references must be basenames.

VERDICT: RICH. Project + current-file basename + language + normalized tool activity + phase (Thinking/Running tools) + elapsed timer (from the user-turn `timestamp`) + model id are all recoverable, locally, in an append-only line-delimited JSONL at a stable path. This matches the Codex / DeepSeek Harness richness level, with the model id as a bonus.

risks: PATH CHURN: the chat log moved from `~/.qwen/tmp/<sha256(cwd)>/chats/` (v0.1.0-v0.3.0) to `~/.qwen/projects/<sanitizeCwd(cwd)>/chats/` (v0.4.0+). Register BOTH roots or older installs go dark.

ROOT RELOCATION: `Storage.getGlobalQwenDir()` honours the `QWEN_HOME` env var and `Storage.getRuntimeBaseDir()` honours `QWEN_RUNTIME_DIR` / the `runtimeOutputDir` setting, so the tree can live outside `%USERPROFILE%\.qwen`. Unverified how common this is; the default-path adapter will simply not find those sessions.

SAME FILE, TWO DIALECTS: for ACP/daemon/worktree sessions the same `<sessionId>.jsonl` holds `managed_session_header_v1` / `managed_session_event_v1` / `managed_session_commit_v1` records (epoch-ms `occurredAt`, free-form `payload`) instead of ChatRecords. The parser must ignore them; if upstream ever defaults to `managed` for plain CLI sessions, tool granularity is lost (fail safe = no events, not wrong events).

PROJECT ID IS A PATH, NOT A HASH: `sanitizeCwd()` lowercases and replaces every non-alphanumeric char with '-', so `c--users-pc-documents-discodex` encodes the whole path. It is lossy/ambiguous; never derive the project name from it — use the record's `cwd`.

THE LOG CONTAINS EVERYTHING: full user prompts, assistant text, and raw tool output are on disk in the same JSONL. A sloppy parser (e.g. using the `thought` text or the `functionResponse.response` as a label) would leak conversation content to Discord. All labels must come from the closed `classify_tool()` table; all paths must be reduced to basenames.

SUBAGENT CORRELATION IS ONLY BEST-EFFORT: the `parent_session` system record carries `parentSessionId` in the CHILD file (not the child id in the parent file), so Discodex's `SubagentSpawned{conversation_id}` mapping (which expects the id to appear in the sub-session's PATH) is not directly satisfiable. `agent_message` records do carry `agentId`+`agentName`, but the exact agentId<->child-file-name correspondence is UNVERIFIED. Ship `AgentDetected` only; do not guess the subagent mapping.
MODEL ID HYGIENE: `model` / `systemPayload.modelId` are free-form strings from upstream config. They must be charset- and length-filtered (like `deepseek_model_label`) before they can reach Discord.

`.runtime.json` IS NOT A LOG: the runtime-status sidecar is atomically REWRITTEN (not appended), is never deleted on /quit or crash, and its `pid` may be dead. It must not be fed to `LogTailer`/`parse_line_for`; if adopted it needs a separate re-read-on-change reader plus a PID-liveness check.

STARTUP SCAN LIMIT: `recent_logs(root, provider, 8)` keeps only the 8 newest logs per source; with many Qwen project dirs, the active session may not be among them. Consider a per-provider larger cap or a most-recent-per-project-dir selection.

summary: Qwen Code (Alibaba) is a Google-Gemini-CLI-derived CLI, published as npm `@qwen-code/qwen-code` (latest 0.25.3; the name `@qwen-code/qwen-cli` does NOT exist — registry 404), with the binary `qwen`. It stores chat history LOCALLY as an append-only, newline-delimited JSONL file at `%USERPROFILE%\.qwen\projects\<sanitized-cwd>\chats\<sessionId>.jsonl` (`.qwen` = `Storage.getGlobalQwenDir()`; `projects/<sanitized-cwd>` = `Storage.getProjectDir()`; `chats/<sessionId>.jsonl` = `ChatRecordingService.ensureChatsDir()/ensureConversationFile()`). Every record is a self-contained `ChatRecord` with `uuid`/`parentUuid`, `sessionId`, an ISO-8601 `timestamp`, `cwd` (the workspace root), `version`, `model`, and `message.parts[]` carrying `functionCall {id,name,args}` (tool start) and `functionResponse {id,name,response}` (tool end). Writes go through `jsonl.writeLine()` = `fs.promises.appendFile(..., {flush:true})` under a per-file mutex — strictly append-only and LIVE, i.e. exactly the shape Discodex's `LogTailer` already handles, so NO watcher rework is needed. Recoverable without shipping any conversation text: project (last segment of `cwd`), model id (`model` / `systemPayload.modelId`), current file basename (from `functionCall.args.file_path`/`path`), normalized tool activity (from `functionCall.name` + `args.command`), phase (user-turn record -> tool call -> `functionResponse` -> `turn_result`), and the elapsed timer (user-turn `timestamp`). Diffs vs Gemini CLI: same ChatRecord lineage but a DIFFERENT on-disk root (`~/.qwen` vs `~/.gemini`) and a DIFFERENT project subdir — Qwen uses a readable `projects/<sanitizeCwd(cwd)>` tree (lowercased path, non-alphanumerics -> '-') while Gemini CLI uses an opaque `tmp/<sha256(cwd)>` hash. Two historical layouts exist (v0.1.0-v0.3.0 used `~/.qwen/tmp/<sha256>/chats/`), so the adapter should watch both roots. The VS Code companion does NOT use `state.vscdb`/`globalStorage` (zero hits in the published bundle) — it talks to the daemon/ACP bridge, so no sqlite crate is needed. A second, non-log artifact exists — `<sessionId>.runtime.json` (pid/session_id/work_dir/started_at/qwen_version), written atomically (REWRITTEN, not appended) for external observers; it is optional and must not be fed to the line tailer. The one real caveat is that a second record dialect ('managed_session_*' events) can appear in the same file for ACP/daemon sessions; the parser should recognize and ignore those subtypes.
